messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Runtime pool us-west-2-runtime-2 reporting a rising rate of OOM exits from the attention pager allocator (kv-slab usage trending upward). 11 node restarts in last 12m. Trigger: OOM_kv_slab_fragmentation >= 10

Sasha O: seeing it. impact: increased 504s for short gen and some hung streams. tagging oncall now.

Arun S: @Sasha O I'm on it — attaching the topline from the runtime logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:12Z] runtime: attention_pager: slab_frag_count=892 free_chunks=12 largest_free=408k total_alloc=75GB
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] cuda: MPS lost context on device 0, code 0x7f
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] runtime: oom: attempted alloc 64MB slab, failed. initiating node restart
```

Arun S: looks like slow fragmentation (small free chunks) + occasional CUDA context errors.

Jon P: any customer-facing errors? which routes affected?

Maya K: VanguardAI (cust-784) and a handful of dev accounts reported 504s between 18:00-18:07. We see an uptick in retries from the router metrics.

Sasha O: mitigation plan — quick live steps: 1) reduce batching to minimum on us-west-2 runtime route 2) temporarily disable attention paging for heavy gen models (config: attention_pager.enabled=false) 3) cordon the top 3 flapping nodes and force GC/evict local KV caches 4) route traffic to us-west-2-runtime-1 (lighter load)

Diego L: on node actions — ssh to node, run: 
```
sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-slab-defrag --aggressive --max-iter 3
journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 | tail -n 80
sudo systemctl start redwood-runtime
```

Diego L: if defrag fails, snapshot logs and keep node cordoned. we don't want noisy restarts.

Taylor R: @Arun @Diego can we push a k8s patch to lower the runtime batch size param globally for the pool? quick helm patch: 
```
helm upgrade redwood-runtime --set runtime.batchSize=1 --namespace runtime-usw2
```

Arun S: doing patch now, staging rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with canary. queueing 10% immediately.

Sasha O: also enable fallback routing policy so requests to heavy models use ded-1 pool if latencies exceed 800ms.

Jon P: customer comms — Maya, can you open an incident status page blurb? short: "Experiencing degraded text-generation on us-west-2; mitigation in progress; some requests may return 504 or increased latency."

Maya K: posting now. linking ticket ENG-7793 and tagging account team.

Arun S: quick triage notes: fragmentation appears to be from many short-lived allocations (prefix cache churn). KV eviction wasn't compacting smaller slabs effectively. We should consider changing allocator to prefer coalescing small free segments.

Diego L: observed CUDA context resets correlate with highest fragmentation windows — could be driver-level interaction when memory pressure spikes. capturing coredumps and kernel logs.

Sasha O: live: 3 nodes cordoned, batch-size patched to 1 at 10% canary, attention pager toggled off for 6 model routes. Early signal: error rate dropping ~35% on canary hosts.

Jon P: good. next steps for post-incident: 1) rollback if unstable, 2) persistent fix: allocator defrag strategy + KV eviction tuning, 3) add automated early warning (fragmentation threshold alert earlier), 4) customer impact RCA and runbook updates.

Arun S: creating ENG-7794 for allocator change and ENG-7795 for alert tuning. will add test harness for long-tail small-allocation workload.

Diego L: collecting node dumps, attaching to ENG-7794. question: do we want a temporary autoscale on the runtime pool to reduce per-node pressure?

Sasha O: yes, request +2 nodes to the pool for 30m to give breathing room. @infra please approve.

Taylor R: infra approved, scaling now.

Maya K: posted customer update: "Mitigations applied; some traffic rerouted; monitoring for stabilization. We'll provide ETA after root cause." customers acknowledged.

Arun S: status in 12m: canary error rate down 60%, overall pool error down 40%, a few remaining nodes showing leak signs. continuing defrag + GC on cordoned nodes.

Sasha O: if stabilization holds, we plan controlled uncordon after defrag passes and node runs 30m stable.

Jon P: remind to preserve logs and snapshots for postmortem, and attach any driver/kernel upgrades if we see pattern.

Maya K: will draft postmortem template and plug metrics. assigning primary authors: Arun S (allocator fix), Diego L (node diagnostics), Sasha O (ops timeline), Jon P (customer impact).

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in-progress — error rate decreasing. PING: handoff if shift change incoming.

Sasha O: I'm handing off to @Jon P for overnight surveillance in 45m. leave the runbook steps in the handoff doc. :thumbsup:

Jon P: acknowledged, picking up. will monitor fragmentation alerts and hold until all cordoned nodes are healthy.

Maya K: closing slack thread for now, will reopen if regressions. adding link to incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ENG-7793

Jon P: final note before wrap — schedule driver checks on next maintenance window; prefer to test newer CUDA driver on a dev cluster before rolling.

Sasha O: copied. good job team. :eyes:
